summary: Revise at 6.2 (round 1: 5.0; author: 6.5; Caiman: 7; ship: 7.5). Every gate is green and verified. Round 1's worst faults are fixed. The composition now follows the plan: heads sit at the arm tips and the bills point outward. The draft release is 0/0. The primaries on the open shoulder are countable true-outline feathers, the best passage on the ring. It still does not pass the glance test, and it is not a raven yet. At 300 px the hero shows a polished egg-shaped dome with a hooked blade in front of it. That could be a bird skull, but it also reads as a beetle, a turtle's head or a claw. The face view shows a black cab on an oval plaque between two smooth helmets. The bills are foreshortened out of sight there, as the author concedes. The heads are the focal point, and they are the weakest modelling on the ring. Each skull is a 5.6 × 2.9 mm featureless polished bulb, taller than its bill root. The eye renders as a curled comma sliver, not an almond, which makes it a poor face. The tip-side flank carries the sheared fold the author reports (shoulder.png, side.png). Around the stone, the 'Collet bed' and the neck feathers render as rows of stepped dashes, a woven or basketry plaque. That is the stair-step look the true-outline rule forbids. At the palm the two tails are rectangular stepped slabs with square ends: mechanical CAD, not rectrices. The silhouette is distinct in the Bestiarium. Density is close to Caiman's, but legibility falls short of it where it matters most, at the heads and the stone. One round remains. Reaching 7.5 needs about +1.3, more than Phoenix gained in any round. It is plausible only because the remaining defects are concrete and local: head sculpt, eye, bill visibility in the face view, the collet plaque, the tails and the fold. If round 3 does not make the face and hero read as two ravens uncaptioned, the ring is cut.
strengths: Composition restored to the plan: Huginn's skull at θ 113.6–139° with the bill to 169°, Muninn mirrored at 66.4–41° to 11°, both bills pointing outward. The round-1 serpent-biting-the-band reading is gone.

Primaries on the side faces (28 stamps, 8.5 × 1.0 mm, 0.25–0.45 mm proud) read as shingled, countable feathers with crisp outlines and graver herringbone inside. The right shoulder of hero.png and the left of shoulder.png are at house density.
The hooked bill is a clean, well-drawn form in profile (shoulder.png, head.png): the arched culmen and the 0.6 mm hook are convincing.
The collet is reduced to a single lip, and the onyx is fully visible in a made bezel with its drill dot kept.
All gates are green, including the draft 768×320 release that failed in round 1. stamps_384 now requires both releases clear. The template is lean: 0 patches and 1.80 MB of the 3 MB budget.
The silhouette is distinct in the Bestiarium: two low domed heads flanking a cab on a crossover. No other ring uses this layout.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Heads, necks, plumage, primaries and tails are all raven, face to palm. The dashed oval 'Collet bed' plaque reads as basketwork rather than plumage, but it is not a foreign motif.

The primaries and hackles are true-outline stamps and render crisp. The painted relief around the stone does not. The 'Collet bed' and the neck feathers between the collet and each skull (θ ≈ 65–80° and 100–115°) render as rows of stepped dashes and ladder rungs (hero.png, stones.png, head.png). The palm tails end in square stair-steps (palm.png). The tip-side skull flank is sheared into a fold (shoulder.png).

checklist.item: Faces and eyes allowed when they read well; a poor face is a defect
checklist.reason: The eye renders as a curled comma or sliver on the skull flank (head.png, hero.png), not the 1.1 × 0.7 almond the report claims. The skull is a featureless polished egg with no brow shadow over the eye. In face.png the two heads read as helmets or beetle shells.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: The onyx sits in a made bezel with a single lip and is fully visible in hero, face and stones. The stones report counts 1, the preview counts 1, and the drill dot is kept. The collet is now subordinate to the heads in the hero.

checklist.item: Shoulder ornament not cut off toward the face
checklist.reason: Plumage and primaries run up to the skulls and the collet on both shoulders. Caveat: the tip-side flank carries only 3 hackles against 7, and the fold interrupts it.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: The palm tails are rectangular stepped slabs with square ends and right-angled notches (palm.png, side.png bottom). The bypass arm end shows as a plain step on the bore side (reverse.png, lower right). The skulls are smooth primitives, not sculpted heads.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable: the base is procedural (LowDome bypass), not factory stock. Bore walls and the comfort edge stay clean.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from the other Bestiarium rings
checklist.reason: Two low heads flanking a cab on a crossover. Manticora's hook stands vertical from a single boss, Fenrir is a full mask, Harpyia has lofted wings, Kraken tentacles and Arachne limbs. No overlap.

checklist.item: Reads as its subject at a glance at 300 px, uncaptioned
checklist.reason: hero-300 reads as 'a bird-ish or beetle-ish hooked head beside a black stone'. face-300 reads as 'a cab between two helmets' with no bills visible. Neither gives 'raven' without the caption. Better than round 1, which read as a serpent, but not there.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The hierarchy exists: heads and collet large, primaries medium, graver barbs small. Density along the shoulders matches Caiman's. But the two largest and most-viewed forms, the skulls, are the barest surfaces on the ring. The dashed plaque around the stone is less legible than Caiman's crisp blocks.

punch_list.zone: Both skulls: layer 'Raven heads', Huginn θ 113.6–139°, Muninn θ 66.4–41°
punch_list.change:
Sculpt the skull into a raven's head rather than an egg.
- Drop the crown from 2.9 mm to 2.2–2.4 mm above the bare crest, so the culmen runs into the forehead in one line. Today the dome stands clearly above the bill root.
- Lengthen the forehead ramp from 0.94 mm to 1.5–2.0 mm.
- Keep the bill root at the forehead's height, with no dip.
- Over the rear 55–60% of each skull (crown, nape and cheek), cast scalloped contour feathers 0.8–1.0 mm across, with strokes of at least 0.35 mm, pointing back along the ring.
- Leave only the forehead and the bill glossy.
- Add a supra-orbital brow ridge 0.25–0.30 mm proud over the eye, running 2.0 mm along the ring.
punch_list.acceptance: head.png: the forehead-to-bill line is continuous with no step at the bill root. At least 12 countable feather scallops cover the rear skull, and there is no polished area wider than 2.5 mm on the skull except the forehead. side.png: the head profile shows the bill, a sloping forehead and a feathered nape on both heads. Field Castable, clamp ≤ 0.05 mm, release 0/0.

punch_list.zone: Eye stamps 'Huginn, eye high/low' and 'Muninn, eye high/low', skull front third
punch_list.acceptance: head.png at 1600 px: the eye's outline is a closed almond with no curl or tail, and it measures 1.0–1.1 × 0.6–0.7 mm against the skull. hero-300: the eye is a readable dark almond under a brow, not a highlight sliver. Parting-monotone, release 0/0.

punch_list.zone: Face view: bills 'Raven heads' layer, Huginn θ 140–169°, Muninn θ 40–11°
punch_list.change:
Make the bills read from the face.
- Move each skull 6–8° toward the collet (Huginn to about θ 107–132°, Muninn to about 73–48°).
- Start each bill at θ 132° or 48°, keeping its 6.0 mm length and its hook.
- Widen the bill root across the band from about 2.35 to 2.8–3.0 mm, tapering to the hook, so its plan-view wedge shows in the face view.
- Carry the culmen ridge (±0.30 flat) as a highlight line.
punch_list.acceptance: face-300.png shows two wedge-shaped bills pointing to 3 and 9 o'clock, each at least 18 px long, with hooks visible. Shown uncaptioned to a fresh reviewer, face-300 and hero-300 are named as birds or ravens, and two heads are counted. Release 0/0 at all three builds.

punch_list.zone: Skull tip-side flanks (Huginn +z, Muninn −z): bypass arm end under each skull at θ ≈ 125° and 55°
punch_list.change: Remove the fold at its source. Adopt the author's opt-in `ShankStyle::bypass_fair_deg`, set to 4–6° on Corvus only. Fence it at format 6, and add a test that every existing bypass design builds byte-identical with the value 0. That is a core change, so get Logan's sign-off first. If it is refused, end the arm tip under the collet instead (BYPASS_TIP within ±25° of top), so no skull sits on the tip's normal swing. Then restore the 7 hackles on the tip-side face.
punch_list.acceptance: shoulder.png and side.png show no crease or sheared band on either skull's tip side. Each head carries 6–8 hackles on both side faces, 20 → 28 hackle stamps in total. Self-crossings 0 and watertight at all three builds, recorded in report.json.

punch_list.zone: Crossing: layer 'Collet bed' (the oval plaque round the onyx) and the neck feathers of 'Raven plumage' at θ ≈ 65–80° and 100–115°
punch_list.change:
Replace the dashed rows, which render as stair-stepped basketwork, with the crossed necks' own contour feathers.
- Scalloped or pointed tips with a true outline, 1.0–1.25 mm pitch, each row stepping at least 0.20 mm.
- Flow from each skull's nape into the collet's foot.
- Drop the plaque's hard oval rim, so the collet rises out of feathers, not out of a plate.
- If painted relief cannot hold the outlines at this pitch, strike them as stamps, like the hackles.
punch_list.acceptance: stones.png at 1600 px shows no dashed rows, ladder rungs or stair-steps round the collet, and at least 10 countable feather tips on each side of the stone. hero.png shows no oval plaque rim. Clamp ≤ 0.05 mm and release 0/0.

punch_list.change:
Turn the stepped slabs into rectrices.
- Round each feather's tip with a radius of half its width (about 0.6 mm), in place of the square end.
- Taper each feather from 1.2 mm at the tip to 0.9 mm at the root.
- Splay the five feathers 4–6° apart, so each tail forms a wedge, not a stacked rectangle.
- Fair the 0.22 mm steps with a 0.15 mm radius at the along-ring edges.
- Close the bare gap between the two tails at θ 270° to 0.3 mm or less, or interleave the tips as the plan specifies.
punch_list.acceptance: palm.png shows two opposed wedges, each with 5 rounded tips and no right-angled corners or notches. side.png shows no notch or crack at the palm. Release 0/0 at θ 240–300° at all three builds.
